key_insight: AISPA shows that commercial AI system prompts increasingly include user-protective instructions, but those protections are uneven, incomplete, and often mixed with instructions that can still harm user interests.
engineering_relevance: For AI product teams, the paper provides a practical audit framework to evaluate system prompts against user-centered safety and accountability goals before deployment.
method: Defined AISPA, a user-centric taxonomy with eight user-relevant dimensions for auditing system prompt instructions.
Manually reviewed 3,249 instructions from system prompts across 88 commercial AI products.
Labeled each instruction as protective or problematic to compare prompt design patterns across products.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products and finds that 98.9% of products include at least one protective instruction, while about 40% also contain at least one problematic instruction.
watch_item: Because system prompts are often undisclosed and auditing depends on available prompt text, the findings may underrepresent hidden or frequently changing prompt behavior.
paper_title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
